name: Null Portrait Series — The Faceless Archive
creator: Collective known as the Hollow Commission
description: A growing archive of large-format physical portraits — painted in oils on salvaged polymer sheeting — depicting people whose identities were erased by corponation legal action, debt enforcement, or identity tier-stripping. Each portrait shows a fully rendered body, clothing, and environment specific to the subject's life, but the face is replaced by a precise void — not blurred or obscured, but physically cut from the material and framed. The archive currently holds 1,847 portraits displayed across underground galleries in Tiers 1 and 2.
medium: physical painting, oil on salvaged polymer
cultural_impact: Has become the primary visual language for the identity rights movement in M88, with the 'hollow face' motif appearing on protest banners, tattoos, and neural feed graphics across all tiers.
controversy: Several subjects have been identified despite the removed faces through contextual details in their portraits, leading to both reunion stories and, in at least two cases, renewed corponation legal pursuit of the subjects.
story_hooks: A character finds a portrait in the archive that is unmistakably of someone they know — someone who told them they were born into a clean identity.

The Hollow Commission is preparing a mass public installation of all 1,847 portraits simultaneously across Meridian 88's public spaces, and they need help coordinating the logistics without corponation detection.
One of the 'erased' subjects whose portrait hangs in the archive is very much alive and very much does not want to be found — by anyone, including the people trying to help them.
